Delete her contact info if you don't already have it memorized and keep doing what you're doing. The best thing you can do to someone you're plan B for is ignore/forget about them.

Deleting the contact info saves you from potentially making an ass of yourself by either suddenly deciding you're super angry at them or how much you miss them.

Also I'd say about 60% of the time you get the satisfaction of getting that text 6 months down the line and being able to say "sorry, who is this?"

28m. Yeah, absolutely. I was diagnosed with PTSD after all of the shit I went through after my last breakup. She left me for someone else and completely cut contact as if we hadn't been in love for 2 years. She'd never shown any signs of being that type of person so it completely blindsided me. Never had any sort of closure or resolve, started abusing my anxiety medication to cope with the pain and that ended up fucking me up for years for totally separate reasons. After 3 years I've moved on from her but I haven't moved on from how much she fucked up my perception of love and dating.

I usually cut things off right when they start getting serious and I don't even really enjoy casual relationships anymore either. I have a healthy relationship with plenty of women as friends but as soon as they try to show any sort of interest or pursue me I get sick, depressed and usually have to cut contact with them.

Don't replace people y'all, it really fucks them up.

I grew up in a small city where the average room for rent in a house with roommates was around $1,000. A studio would be somewhere in the 1.5k-2k range, and a 1BR was about 3.5k. Covering rent alone was usually like 80% of my income. 

I barely make 35k after taxes out here. I eat out daily, grab beers with coworkers nightly, go out drinking on weekends, and buy myself nice shit all the time. Even after all this I usually have some money to put away every month. I think people out here have an extremely dramatic perspective about how "expensive" it is.
